rationale: Full-text review of botanical BDNF modulation examines Salvia miltiorrhiza Bunge (red sage root, Danshen) rather than culinary fresh Salvia officinalis and cites pain only for a separate polyphenol blend.

Full-text review covers antinociceptive animal models of Neotropical Salvia subgenus Calosphace species (S. amarissima, S. semiatrata, S. divinorum, S. tiliifolia) rather than fresh culinary Salvia officinalis or Parkinson pain.

Full-text mouse formalin assay tests isolated oral sclareol from Salvia sclarea (clary sage, different species and isolated constituent from fresh culinary Salvia officinalis), reporting lower paw licking and edema (with 2026 journal batch corrigendum PMID:42898092).
Full-text review examines tanshinone diterpenoids from Salvia miltiorrhiza (Danshen) root in preclinical neuropathic pain rather than fresh culinary Salvia officinalis or Parkinson pain.
Full-text horticultural production survey of Jammu, Kashmir and Ladakh mentions citrus crop output and uses falls strictly for climatic zone and annual rainfall, with no human fall outcome.

Full-text human sleep study tests inhaled orange essential-oil odor via nose clips in 139 healthy adults; all fall occurrences refer solely to falling asleep, with no oral raw orange intake or fall-frequency endpoint.
Full-text plant genetics paper sequences Citrus mitochondrial introns; fall refers to taxonomic placement within Citrus and Parkinson is an author citation (Parkinson et al., 2005).

Full-text plant physiology study tests soil glomalin protein on lemon and trifoliate orange seedlings; fall refers to sucrose-droplet water-potential assay and Parkinson is a chemical method citation (Parkinson and Allen).
Full-text computational molecular docking and MD simulation examines isolated hesperidin binding to alpha-synuclein fibrils in silico, with no whole raw orange exposure or human/animal fall outcome.

Full-text hesperidin review cites one preliminary human elderly fall-risk trial (Altemor multi-ingredient hesperidin, diosmin and proanthocyanidins supplement, n = 36, PMID:40694049 / NCT06352099) and flags human evidence as underpowered without isolating raw orange or testing Parkinson falls.

Abstract-level mechanistic review of isolated citrus flavanone naringenin across neurodegenerative pathways (PMC full text not open-access via API); does not test raw orange consumption or clinical fall frequency.

Full-text review of estrogenic plants for menopausal cognition discusses Salvia officinalis aqueous-ethanolic extract strictly for hot flashes and ERLUX estrogenicity and mentions cogwheel rigidity only in the textbook definition of Parkinson disease.
Full-text review covers Ziziphus mucronata (buffalo-thorn, Rhamnaceae) traditional African medicinal uses rather than Phoenix dactylifera culinary dried date fruit.

Full-text rat scopolamine memory study tests Ziziphus jujuba leaf extract (jujube, Rhamnaceae, distinct genus from Phoenix dactylifera date fruit), uses date as a temporal phrase, and conducts no pain assay.

Full-text dairy nutraceuticals narrative review mentions calcium-enriched orange juice only in passing as an example nutraceutical and links constipation relief to dairy and probiotic functional foods rather than raw orange.

Full-text flavonoid review discusses orange-juice hesperidin pharmacokinetics and preclinical PD models, citing constipation only in a general gut-dysbiosis paragraph referencing a separate prebiotic trial (UG1601) rather than raw orange.
Full-text mouse formalin paw-edema assay tests isolated sclareol from Salvia sclarea (not fresh culinary Salvia officinalis) and contains zero fatigue measurements.

Full-text review covers tanshinones from Salvia miltiorrhiza (Danshen) root (citing a rodent forced-swim endurance test of tanshinone IIA), not culinary fresh Salvia officinalis or human Parkinson fatigue.

Abstract-level pharmacology review covers Salvia divinorum hallucinogen salvinorin A (kappa-opioid agonist, distinct psychoactive species from culinary dried Salvia officinalis; PMC body not open-access via API), with no Parkinson apathy outcome.
